docs.title: The system philosophy
docs.text:
This chapter explains the product bet, why responsibilities are split across four layers, and which invariants and trade-offs follow. The next chapter names the components; the workflow chapter owns the request-by-request journey.

You do not need to know the codebase. By the end you will have a small vocabulary — sketch, artifact, Capability, Plan, intent — and a picture of four layers that everything else hangs on.

docs.title: The core bet
docs.text:
Imagine a spreadsheet of invoices on your laptop. You want to ask “What is total revenue by country?” You do not want to upload the file to someone else’s warehouse. You also do not want a chatbot that invents a number.

nolainquery’s bet is: local computation, remote reasoning.

Your machine keeps the file, derives a compact description of it, runs whatever analysis comes back, and shows the result. The remote service does not receive the full dataset. It sees a sketch — column names, types, summaries, and, on clients that include them, a bounded set of sample rows or values — plus your question. It returns artifacts: executable analysis, and if you asked for them, a computation graph and a chart contract. Your machine runs those artifacts against the real file.

The analogy is a librarian and a reading room. You do not ship the books to a consultant. You send the card catalog. The consultant writes a procedure (“pull these shelves, add these columns, rank the result”). You run the procedure in the room that actually has the books. The answer is true because it was computed there, not because the consultant asserted it.

That split is the product. Everything below is how the split is kept reliable, cheap enough, and hard to misuse.

docs.title: Four layers
docs.text:
Think of four floors, from closest to you (and to the file) to farthest from the data.

Local layer          owns the file, derives the sketch, runs artifacts, shows results
Dialogue layer       decides whether this turn should generate anything
Synthesis layer      once admitted, produces typed artifacts
Settlement layer     who is calling, which model, what the reasoning costs

The data plane is the local layer: own the file, compute, report. The control plane is dialogue + synthesis + settlement: reason, admit, charge. The sketch is the only interface between them. If a change requires the control plane to see more of the file, it is fighting this design.

docs.title: Local layer
docs.text:
The local layer owns the file, derives the sketch, executes artifacts, and shows results. It is the only layer that may touch the complete dataset and the only one whose output counts as an answer grounded in real rows.

It does not invent analysis, call models, or decide product scope. This makes privacy structural, while accepting that a thin sketch can hide file-specific quirks from remote reasoning.

docs.title: Dialogue layer
docs.text:
The dialogue layer treats each user message as a conversation decision, not an automatic generation request. It can answer from the sketch, explain a prior result, refuse unsupported work, ask for clarification, or admit generation.

It does not select pipelines or optional artifacts. The gate saves unnecessary generation and keeps product scope explicit, but adds model calls and can make the conversation unavailable when classification fails.

docs.title: Synthesis layer
docs.text:
Once generation is admitted, the synthesis layer produces typed artifacts under a registered Capability, through a Plan. Three terms carry this model through the rest of the book:

  • A Capability is a product on the menu. Today: “descriptive analysis of one file.”
  • A Plan is a kitchen line for that product. Today: the Pandas line. Another line (Ibis) is catalogued and refused until it is implemented.
  • A Stage is a station on that line. Stations consume and produce artifacts. Optional artifacts (graph, chart) are request options on a Plan, not extra menu items.

Policy constructs the pipeline; the model fills artifacts rather than designing the production line. This keeps optional outputs composable, though derived graph and chart artifacts can still drift from the executable code.

docs.title: Settlement layer
docs.text:
The settlement layer identifies the caller, exposes the model catalog, and charges for remote reasoning as model calls complete. It does not execute data or decide which questions are in scope.

Charging by call follows actual provider cost, so two apparently similar questions can cost different amounts when models, optional artifacts, or failure paths differ.

docs.title: Durable invariants
docs.text: The implementation can evolve without changing the product’s identity only while these boundaries remain true.

docs.title: Data stays local
docs.text:
• The complete file stays on the user’s machine.
  • The cloud receives only the question and a sketch. Because sketches may contain bounded sample values, this is data minimization rather than a claim that no row values ever leave the machine.
  • Cloud artifacts are proposals. The answer becomes grounded only when the local layer executes them against the real file.

docs.title: Policy remains authoritative
docs.text:
• Models may classify, interpret, and propose; registered policy decides what can run.
  • Conversation intent is not a generation Capability. A message can be useful without creating analysis.
  • Optional graphs and chart contracts are outputs of a Plan, not new products invented by a prompt.
  • A normal conversation turn must pass classification. If that machinery fails, the request stops with HTTP 503 instead of failing open into generation.

docs.title: Generated work remains bounded
docs.text:
• Executable analysis is primary; graph and chart artifacts are derived.
  • Static checks precede delivery, but execution against the full dataset remains local.
  • Repair is feedback about execution, not permission to reinterpret the question or switch products.
  • Retries and cancellation are bounded. Their exact budgets and stage behavior belong in The parts of the system.

docs.title: Cost follows remote reasoning
docs.text:
• Each completed model call is charged as reasoning work; queueing and local execution are not cloud charges.
  • Work already completed remains chargeable even if a later stage fails or the caller cancels.
  • A caller without spending authority does not enter paid reasoning work.

docs.title: Strengths, assumptions, tradeoffs
docs.text:
Strengths. Structural privacy. Answers grounded in execution. A conversation that can refuse. A small, explicit product surface. Deterministic belts around generative steps. Cost aligned with work.

Assumptions. The sketch is representative enough, often enough. A single executable-analysis engine is a sufficient lingua franca between control plane and data plane. The desktop is a trusted partner: it executes, it reports, it owns optional-artifact toggles. Bounded retries and a required classifier gate are preferable to unclassified generation. Users will accept paying for the gate and for failed steps because those were real model calls.

Choice What it buys What it costs Sketch only, never the file Privacy, simpler trust, local truth Missed quirks; generation can be locally wrong Intent gate before generation Cheap refusals; clearer product boundary Extra calls; classifier failure makes the turn unavailable Classifier suggests, policy admits The model cannot invent pipelines Catalog and policy must stay the real source of truth Optional artifacts, not extra Plans One Plan, many outputs Options must be carried on every turn Analysis first, graph and chart derived Fast path to something executable Drift between code, graph, and spec Repair without re-classifying Fast correction on exec errors Repair cannot change the question’s meaning Charge every model call immediately Matches vendor cost Users pay for failed steps and for the gate itself Short-lived session memory Simple operations History is not a durable account object Single enabled Capability Honest “out of scope” Dialogue must keep saying no Direct generation beside conversation Same artifacts without a chat Two paths that can drift if they are not kept honest

docs.title: Room for improvement
docs.text:
The current shape is a working compromise, not a finished architecture.

The sketch is still a sketch. Better summaries, better samples, and honest signals about data quality would raise hit rate without moving the file.

One Capability is both a strength and a ceiling. “Out of scope” is doing a lot of work. A second product will test whether intent, policy, and artifacts actually compose.

A second engine is a promise. Until another Plan is implemented, “Plan = engine” is vocabulary, not a proven split.

Code, graph, and chart can disagree. Treating the graph as a projection is convenient. Making it the executable source of truth would make the canvas trustworthy. That is not done.

Dialogue is a good gate and a weak memory. Sessions expire, ownership is bound to the API key that created them, and follow-up quality depends on whatever was last stored.

Wording-based safety duplicates part of the catalog boundary. Classifier failure already stops the turn. Out-of-scope behavior can become more uniform when the Capability catalog replaces the remaining phrase lists.

Settlement is call-shaped; the product is still question-shaped. Clearer receipts and budgets per question would make “pay for reasoning” feel like a product.

The local layer is trusted more than it is isolated. Policy can constrain what ships; it cannot make local execution a full sandbox of an untrusted world.

The next chapter, The parts of the system, takes this design and names the components: desktop, local engine, Cloud API, generation pipeline, and how a Capability is admitted. After that, A conversation from start to finish walks one question through every HTTP step the desktop actually takes.

docs.title: Calling the Cloud API
docs.text:
The previous chapters explained what nolainquery is and how a question travels through it. This chapter is the HTTP reference: how a caller authenticates, which doors exist, and what a request looks like.

There are two doors into the same product.

  • Conversation is what the desktop uses. You open a session on a sketch, send a message, and the server decides whether to reply in text, ask a clarifying question, or queue a generation job. After local execution you report the outcome; the server may repair. This is the full loop in A conversation from start to finish.
  • Direct generation skips the session and the gate. You admit a Capability, poll for artifacts, and execute them yourself. Same dishes, no maître d’, no repair loop.

Both doors receive a sketch (metadata), never the complete file. A sketch can contain real sample values; its exact construction and current desktop serialization are documented in Sketch and metadata. Both doors return artifacts: Pandas code, and optionally a computation graph and a chart contract. Interactive OpenAPI lives at http://localhost:8000/docs.

Examples below use local development URLs. Configure the caller’s base URL for the environment you operate. The canonical product domain is https://nolainquery.com; this repository does not establish whether a particular hosted API deployment is currently available.

Related chapters: Credits (what a call costs), A conversation from start to finish (the desktop loop and status fields).

docs.title: Endpoint index
docs.text: Area Current routes Status GET /, GET /health Catalogs GET /api/v1/llm/models, GET /api/v1/capabilities Conversation POST /api/v1/conversation/start, /message, /result, /synthesize; GET or DELETE /api/v1/conversation/{session_id} Generation POST /api/v2/generate_dag; legacy POST /api/v1/generate_dag; POST /api/v1/analyze_query Jobs GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id}, POST /api/v1/cancel_task/{task_id} Account GET /api/auth/me, GET or POST /api/auth/keys, DELETE /api/auth/keys/{key_id}, GET /api/auth/key-status Billing POST /api/billing/stripe/checkout, POST /api/billing/stripe/webhook

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Cloud workflow, catalog, generation, and billing-checkout routes carry an API key:

-H "X-API-Key: <your-api-key>"

Keys come from the nolainquery portal, or from POST /api/auth/keys once you are signed in. Portal account routes under /api/auth/* use a Supabase access token instead:

-H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"

GET /api/auth/key-status also authenticates with X-API-Key. The Stripe webhook is the unauthenticated exception under /api/billing/*; it verifies Stripe’s signature instead.

docs.title: Who may spend credits
docs.text:
Consumption is account-based for portal-linked keys. Admission reads the profile balance and returns 402 Payment Required when it is empty.

Key type Admitted? Charged per model call? Portal-linked (user_id set) Requires remaining credits Yes Unlinked owner (tier = owner, no user_id) Always No Unlinked non-owner 402 —

The repository declares monthly targets of 1,000 credits for Free and 50,000 for Premium, but it does not contain the automation that grants or resets those amounts. See Credits.

Queueing a job does not consume credits by itself. Each model call is charged from token usage plus surplus as soon as it completes.

All model traffic routes through OpenRouter. Pass an optional model field (a catalog id from GET /api/v1/llm/models); omit it to use the server default.

docs.title: Health and catalogs
docs.text: These endpoints do not generate analysis. They tell you whether the system is up, which models you may pick, and which products the server currently admits.

docs.title: GET / — service status
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8000/

{
  "app": "Data Query DAG Generator API",
  "status": "online",
  "documentation": "/docs"
}

docs.title: GET /health — runtime health
docs.text:
Reports Redis, Celery workers, and Supabase. Generation endpoints return 503 when Redis or a worker is unavailable.

curl http://localhost:8000/health

{
  "status": "ok",
  "services": {
    "redis": { "ok": true },
    "celery": { "ok": true, "workers": ["celery@host"] },
    "supabase": { "ok": true, "host": "your-project.supabase.co" }
  }
}

status is "degraded" when any listed service is not ok.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/llm/models — model catalog
docs.text:
Lists selectable models and the server default. Authentication only; does not require remaining credits.

curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/llm/models \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here"

{
  "provider": "openrouter",
  "default_model_id": "deepseek-v4-flash-0731",
  "models": [
    { "id": "deepseek-v4-flash-0731", "label": "DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731)", "openrouter_model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731", "default": true },
    { "id": "gpt-5.6-luna", "label": "GPT-5.6 Luna", "openrouter_model": "openai/gpt-5.6-luna" }
  ]
}

This model catalog is illustrative and abbreviated. Use the endpoint response for the selectable models and current default.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/capabilities — Capability / Plan catalog
docs.text:
Lists registered generation products, their engines, and optional artifacts. Optional artifacts (graph, chart contract) are request options on a Plan, not extra Plan ids.

curl http://localhost:8000/api/v1/capabilities \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here"

{
  "capabilities": [
    {
      "id": "data_analysis",
      "enabled": true,
      "plans": [
        {
          "plan_id": "data_analysis/pandas",
          "selectable": true,
          "default": true,
          "implemented": true,
          "engine": "pandas",
          "stages": ["generate_pandas", "compile_dag", "format_visualization", "validate_visualization", "validate_dag", "finalize_plan"],
          "optional_stages": ["compile_dag", "format_visualization", "validate_visualization"],
          "optional_artifacts": ["dag", "visualization_spec"],
          "terminal_artifact_kinds": ["code_pandas", "dag", "visualization_spec"]
        },
        {
          "plan_id": "data_analysis/ibis",
          "selectable": false,
          "implemented": false
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

This Capability response is illustrative and abbreviated. Use the endpoint response for current registration and selectability.

data_analysis/ibis is catalogued but not selectable. Older Plan ids such as data_analysis/analysis/with_dag map onto data_analysis/pandas plus options.

docs.title: Conversation: the desktop loop
docs.text: This is the path A conversation from start to finish described. Sessions live in Redis for 24 hours. Every operation loads an owned session: another API key receives 403, while a missing session receives 404.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/conversation/start
docs.text:
Creates a session. No model call; no charge.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/conversation/start \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{ "metadata": { "available_columns": ["Country", "Price"] } }'

{ "session_id": "c0a1b2c3-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef1234567890" }

docs.title: POST /api/v1/conversation/message
docs.text:
The main decision: classify the turn (unless you are answering a clarification) and maybe admit a job.

Field Type Required Description session_id string yes From /start message string yes The user’s text metadata object yes The sketch (see Sketch and metadata) model string no Catalog model id clarifications array no When set, skips classify/semantic and queues generation compile_dag boolean no Compile-DAG toggle (default true) include_visualization boolean no Request a chart spec (default true) plan_id string no Optional catalog Plan (default data_analysis/pandas)

The graph and chart toggles are yours. The classifier may suggest a Capability and a Plan; it does not override these options.

Without clarifications, the server normally makes a classifier model call, including for metadata questions, and returns one of:

type in response Meaning text_response Off-topic, unsafe, underspecified, explanation, out of scope, or semantic failure meta_answer Structure question answered from the sketch clarification Ambiguous terms; resend with clarifications generation Job accepted; poll task_id 
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/conversation/message \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "session_id": "c0a1b2c3-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "message": "Show a bar chart of the top 5 countries by total revenue",
    "metadata": { "available_columns": ["Country", "Quantity", "Price"] },
    "compile_dag": true
  }'

{
  "type": "generation",
  "task_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "session_id": "c0a1b2c3-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "capability_id": "data_analysis",
  "plan_id": "data_analysis/pandas",
  "compile_dag": true,
  "include_visualization": true
}

Requests no registered Capability can serve return text_response and do not queue generation. Forecasting, statistical inference, optimization, and anomaly detection currently fall in that branch. Explanation requests return grounded text from saved result context and do not queue generation. Classifier model unavailability or unusable classifier output instead returns HTTP 503; it does not fail open into generation.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/conversation/result
docs.text:
Notify the server of local execution so follow-ups have context. No charge on a successful store.

When exec_error and pandas_code are set, the previous generation job succeeded, that job still has pandas_retries_left > 0, and the chain has not reached its attempt ceiling, the server queues a repair job (same question, failed code plus traceback, no classifier). Jobs that already failed in the cloud are not re-queued as runtime repairs. The response:

{
  "status": "repairing",
  "type": "generation",
  "task_id": "...",
  "session_id": "...",
  "capability_id": "data_analysis",
  "plan_id": "data_analysis/pandas",
  "compile_dag": true,
  "include_visualization": true,
  "pandas_retries_left": 1
}

Poll that task_id and re-execute locally. If no retries remain, the response is { "status": "ok" }.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/conversation/result \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "session_id": "c0a1b2c3-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "dag": { "graph_id": "...", "nodes": [], "output_node": "node_2" },
    "exec_result": { "preview": [{"Country": "United Kingdom", "revenue": 912345.0}] },
    "pandas_code": "result = df.groupby('Country')['Quantity'].sum()"
  }'

docs.title: POST /api/v1/conversation/synthesize
docs.text:
Optional post-execution framing. Charges credits if a model is invoked. On failure the endpoint still returns { "status": "success", "narrative": {} }.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/conversation/synthesize \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "session_id": "c0a1b2c3-d4e5-6789-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "question": "What are the top 5 countries by total revenue?",
    "result_summary": "United Kingdom leads, followed by France.",
    "outcome": "answered",
    "model": "deepseek-v4-flash-0731"
  }'

docs.title: GET / DELETE /api/v1/conversation/{session_id}
docs.text: Read or delete the Redis session. Delete returns { "status": "deleted" }. Missing sessions return 404. A valid key that does not own the session returns 403 for either method.

docs.title: Direct generation
docs.text:
Use this door when you already know you want artifacts and do not need a chat. Prefer POST /api/v2/generate_dag. The v1 endpoint is a legacy planner → compiler chain that does not use the Capability registry.

Both are asynchronous: they return a task_id. Poll GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id} (next section) for artifacts.

docs.title: POST /api/v2/generate_dag — registered Capability
docs.text:
Admits data_analysis. The server builds a Plan of stages from request options. The Pandas Plan always produces executable code. Optional stages add a graph and/or a chart contract. Each worker model call is charged as it completes; poll billing.charged_credits for the running total.

Stations, in order, when every optional is on:

  1. Write Pandas code from the question and the sketch. Compatibility patches and a static sandbox check (no execution on the server). Truncated, empty, illegal, or incomplete code is rejected and may retry.
  2. Compile a computation graph from that code (compile_dag=true, default). The artifact kind is dag; status responses expose its payload as graph.
  3. Write a chart contract (include_visualization=true, default).
  4. Validate the chart contract.
  5. Validate the graph.
  6. Persist artifacts and finish.

A chart is a toggle, not a different Plan.

Field Type Required Description query string yes Natural-language question metadata object yes The sketch model string no Catalog model id clarifications array no { "term": "...", "chosen_interpretation": "..." } compile_dag boolean no Include the graph (default true) include_visualization boolean no Include a chart contract (default true) capability_id string no Registered Capability (default data_analysis) plan_id string no Catalog Plan (default data_analysis/pandas) 
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v2/generate_dag \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "query": "What are the top 5 countries by total revenue for high-volume transactions?",
    "metadata": {
      "available_columns": ["Invoice", "StockCode", "Description", "Quantity", "InvoiceDate", "Price", "Customer ID", "Country"],
      "sample_data": [
        { "Invoice": "489434", "StockCode": "85048", "Description": "15CM CHRISTMAS GLASS BALL 20 LIGHTS", "Quantity": 12, "InvoiceDate": "2009-12-01 07:45:00", "Price": 6.95, "Customer ID": 13085.0, "Country": "United Kingdom" }
      ],
      "column_semantics": {
        "Invoice": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 28816, "sample_values": ["489434"], "data_type": "string", "semantic_type": "identifier" },
        "StockCode": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 4631, "sample_values": ["85048"], "data_type": "string", "semantic_type": "categorical" },
        "Description": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 4681, "sample_values": ["15CM CHRISTMAS GLASS BALL 20 LIGHTS"], "data_type": "string", "semantic_type": "categorical" },
        "Quantity": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 500, "sample_values": [12], "data_type": "int", "semantic_type": "numeric" },
        "InvoiceDate": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 25210, "sample_values": ["2009-12-01 07:45:00"], "data_type": "date", "semantic_type": "temporal" },
        "Price": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 1606, "sample_values": [6.95], "data_type": "float", "semantic_type": "numeric" },
        "Customer ID": { "null_ratio": 0.21, "cardinality": 4383, "sample_values": [13085.0], "data_type": "float", "semantic_type": "categorical" },
        "Country": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 37, "sample_values": ["United Kingdom"], "data_type": "string", "semantic_type": "categorical" }
      }
    },
    "model": "deepseek-v4-flash-0731",
    "compile_dag": true,
    "include_visualization": true,
    "clarifications": [
      {
        "term": "revenue",
        "chosen_interpretation": "Quantity multiplied by Price"
      },
      {
        "term": "high-volume",
        "chosen_interpretation": "Transactions where Quantity is greater than 100"
      }
    ]
  }'

{
  "status": "queued",
  "task_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "capability_id": "data_analysis",
  "plan_id": "data_analysis/pandas",
  "compile_dag": true,
  "include_visualization": true,
  "stages": ["generate_pandas", "compile_dag", "format_visualization", "validate_visualization", "validate_dag", "finalize_plan"],
  "message": "Poll status via GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id}"
}

Current admission normalizes an unknown or disabled capability_id to data_analysis and an unknown plan_id to the default Pandas Plan. The known but unimplemented data_analysis/ibis Plan returns 400. Redis or Celery unavailability returns 503.

Poll responses include capability_id, plan_id, current_stage, the toggles, pandas_code, optional graph / visualization_spec, and an optional artifacts[] envelope. Reliability fields:

  • pandas_retries_left — remaining local-runtime repair jobs
  • pandas_sandbox_retries_left — remaining in-cloud retries
  • pandas_attempts_used / pandas_total_max_attempts — chain usage and ceiling
  • generation_attempts — per-call diagnostics (finish reason, selected profile, tokens, outcome)

The configured Pandas budgets are: sandbox retries 2, syntax-repair retries 1, local-runtime repairs 2, and a chain-wide generation-attempt ceiling of 9. Compiler and visualization retries use the separate max_retries budget of 2.

Direct generation does not run the conversation repair loop. Reporting POST /api/v1/conversation/result is a conversation-only move.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/generate_dag — legacy planner → compiler
docs.text:
Starts the older background chain (planner text → graph). Prefer v2 or conversation for the registered Capability.

Field Type Required Description query string yes Natural-language question metadata object yes The sketch model string no Catalog model id n_interpretations int no Interpretations for the planner step clarifications array no { "term": "...", "chosen_interpretation": "..." }

The request body has the same sketch shape as v2. The response is { "status": "queued", "task_id": "..." }.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/analyze_query — semantic analysis only
docs.text:
Looks at a question for ambiguous concepts (polysemy, granularity, vagueness) without generating code. Charges for the model call(s) it makes. The same step inside POST /conversation/message is also charged when it invokes a model.

Field Type Required Description query string yes Natural-language question metadata object yes The sketch model string no Catalog model id n_interpretations int no Candidate interpretations per ambiguity (default 4) 
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/analyze_query \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "query": "What are the top 5 countries by total revenue for high-volume transactions?",
    "metadata": {
      "available_columns": ["Invoice", "StockCode", "Description", "Quantity", "InvoiceDate", "Price", "Customer ID", "Country"],
      "sample_data": [
        { "Invoice": "489434", "StockCode": "85048", "Description": "15CM CHRISTMAS GLASS BALL 20 LIGHTS", "Quantity": 12, "InvoiceDate": "2009-12-01 07:45:00", "Price": 6.95, "Customer ID": 13085.0, "Country": "United Kingdom" }
      ],
      "column_semantics": {
        "Country": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 37, "sample_values": ["United Kingdom"], "data_type": "string", "semantic_type": "categorical" },
        "Quantity": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 500, "sample_values": [12], "data_type": "int", "semantic_type": "numeric" },
        "Price": { "null_ratio": 0.0, "cardinality": 1606, "sample_values": [6.95], "data_type": "float", "semantic_type": "numeric" }
      }
    },
    "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
    "n_interpretations": 5
  }'

docs.title: GET /api/v1/get_task_status/{task_id}
docs.text:
Checks progress and retrieves artifacts. Authentication only, so you can still read work that already started after credits are exhausted. Jobs remain in Redis for one hour. The caller must own the job; another valid key receives 403, and an expired or unknown job receives 404.

curl -X GET http://localhost:8000/api/v1/get_task_status/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here"

Useful dag_status values: queued, generating_code, compiling_from_code, formatting_visualization, validating_visualization, validating, finalizing, success, failed, cancelled.

A successful v2 / conversation poll can look like the abbreviated, illustrative response below:

{
  "task_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
  "execution_status": "SUCCESS",
  "dag_status": "success",
  "graph": {
    "graph_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
    "nodes": [
      {
        "id": "node_0",
        "op": "filter_extract",
        "params": { "column": "Quantity", "operator": "gt", "value": 100 },
        "inputs": []
      }
    ],
    "output_node": "node_0"
  },
  "errors": [],
  "pandas_code": "result = df.loc[df['Quantity'] > 100].groupby('Country')['revenue'].sum().nlargest(5)",
  "visualization_spec": {
    "version": 1,
    "kind": "bar",
    "title": "Top 5 countries by revenue",
    "x": "Country",
    "y": ["revenue"],
    "sort_direction": "desc"
  },
  "capability_id": "data_analysis",
  "plan_id": "data_analysis/pandas",
  "compile_dag": true,
  "include_visualization": true,
  "billing": {
    "token_credits": 8,
    "surplus_credits": 8,
    "charged_credits": 16,
    "llm_calls": 4,
    "surplus_rate": 1.0
  },
  "artifacts": [
    { "kind": "code_pandas", "schema_version": 1, "storage_key": "pandas_code", "payload": "..." },
    { "kind": "dag", "schema_version": 1, "storage_key": "graph", "payload": {} },
    { "kind": "visualization_spec", "schema_version": 1, "storage_key": "visualization_spec", "payload": {} }
  ]
}

When compile_dag=false, graph is omitted and pandas_code is the executable artifact. When include_visualization=false, visualization_spec is omitted.

Execute artifacts on the local engine (port 8001): POST /execute_pandas and, when a graph is present, POST /execute_dag.

docs.title: POST /api/v1/cancel_task/{task_id}
docs.text:
Cooperative cancellation between Plan stages. Model calls already completed keep their charges. Restricted to the API key that owns the job.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/cancel_task/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here"
HTTP Meaning 200 Cancellation recorded 403 Key does not own this job 404 Job not found 409 Job can no longer be cancelled

docs.title: GET /api/auth/key-status
docs.text:
Validates an API key (no credit enforcement) and returns whether it can currently spend. Used by desktop Settings.

curl http://localhost:8000/api/auth/key-status \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here"

{
  "tier": "free",
  "masked_key": "sk-free-****7890",
  "credit_balance": 42,
  "can_consume": true,
  "is_active": true,
  "label": "Laptop"
}

credit_balance is null for unlinked keys. can_consume is true for unlinked owner developer keys even then.

Portal account routes use a Supabase Bearer token:

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/auth/me Return the signed-in profile, active keys, and balance GET /api/auth/keys List active keys owned by the signed-in user POST /api/auth/keys Create a free-tier key; returns the full key once DELETE /api/auth/keys/{key_id} Deactivate an owned key; returns 204

docs.title: Stripe top-ups (/api/billing/*)
docs.text:
Requires server-side Stripe configuration on the Cloud API host.

POST /api/billing/stripe/checkout creates a Checkout Session. Requires a portal-linked API key and a price_id for a package configured by the service operator. The backend route exists, but the current portal has no self-service purchase control.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/billing/stripe/checkout \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk-your-key-here" \
  -d '{
    "price_id": "price_basic",
    "success_url": "https://nolainquery.com/billing/success",
    "cancel_url": "https://nolainquery.com/billing/cancel"
  }'

{ "checkout_url": "https://checkout.stripe.com/...", "session_id": "cs_..." }

POST /api/billing/stripe/webhook is the Stripe webhook (no API key). It grants credits on checkout.session.completed when payment succeeds and metadata matches a configured package.

docs.title: Metadata object
docs.text: metadata is the sketch supplied to conversation, semantic-analysis, and generation requests. The API accepts a JSON object; current producers and consumers use conventional fields rather than a dedicated Pydantic model. See Sketch and metadata for the exact sidecar shape, desktop field selection, sample behavior, and privacy implications.

docs.title: Clarifications array
docs.text:
Resolves an ambiguous term to a specific interpretation.

[
  {
    "term": "loyalty",
    "chosen_interpretation": "Count of unique Invoice per Customer ID"
  }
]

docs.title: Visualization spec
docs.text:
A data-free chart contract. The local engine supplies rows at execution time. Supported kind values: line, bar, area, scatter, pie.

{
  "version": 1,
  "kind": "bar",
  "title": "Top 5 countries by revenue",
  "x": "Country",
  "y": ["revenue"],
  "series": null,
  "sort_by": "revenue",
  "sort_direction": "desc",
  "x_label": "Country",
  "y_label": "Revenue"
}

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
HTTP When 400 Invalid request option or known but unimplemented Plan; unknown v2 ids may be normalized to current defaults 401 Missing X-API-Key 402 No credits remaining, or unlinked non-owner key 403 Invalid or deactivated key, or access to another key’s session or job 404 Session or generation job not found 409 Job can no longer be cancelled 500 Task or agent failure; or poll dag_status: "failed" 503 Required runtime/auth/model service unavailable, including classifier failure

When a portal-linked key has no remaining credits, or a non-owner key has no portal account, most workflow endpoints return 402 before they run — including conversation start/message, metadata answers, and synthesis. Unlinked owner developer keys are exempt. Status poll and cancel remain available.

docs.title: Local services, for orientation
docs.text:
The local engine is a separate FastAPI process, normally bound to 127.0.0.1:8001. When NOLAIN_SIDECAR_TOKEN is configured, every request must include X-Nolain-Sidecar-Token. Its current endpoints are:

| Endpoint | Role | | --- | --- | --- | | GET /, GET /health | Local process status | | GET /data_summary | Derive the sketch from source_path | | POST /execute_pandas | Execute generated Pandas code against source_path | | POST /execute_dag | Execute a computation graph (dag artifact) against source_path | | POST /export_transformation | Execute a safe transformation and write a copy beside the source | | GET /preview_data | Return a bounded page or sample for the local spreadsheet view | | GET /column_values | Return bounded distinct values for one column | | POST /tile_data | Compute an exact dashboard-tile aggregation locally | | GET /insights_data | Compute local KPI data |

Cloud API development URLs are http://localhost:8000, with Swagger UI at /docs and ReDoc at /redoc. Local engine inputs include filesystem paths and are intended for the trusted desktop-side process, not the public Cloud API.

For measured worker costs on real question sets, see Query costs.

docs.title: Sketch and metadata
docs.text: nolainquery sends a compact description of a local dataset to the Cloud API instead of uploading the complete file. This description is the sketch. It gives the model enough schema context to generate analysis, but it is not anonymous: sample rows and sample values can contain real data.

docs.title: Where the sketch comes from
docs.text:
The local engine reads the selected path through:

GET http://localhost:8001/data_summary?source_path=...

The response wraps the sketch as {"status":"success","summary":{...}}. For CSV files, the engine uses a reservoir sample of up to 1,000 rows for semantic inference and returns at most 10 of those rows as sample_data. For Parquet files, it inspects the first 1,000 rows and returns the first 10. For Excel, it inspects up to 1,000 rows from the first sheet and returns a sample of at most 10. These limits describe the current sidecar implementation, not a guarantee that every client serializes every field to the cloud.

docs.title: Conventional fields
docs.text:
Cloud request schemas accept metadata as a JSON object rather than enforcing a dedicated metadata model. Current components recognize these fields:

Field Meaning available_columns Ordered column names column_semantics Per-column inferred type, semantic type, null ratio, bounded cardinality, and sample values when available sample_data Optional bounded sample rows total_rows / total_rows_read Optional row-count fields used by metadata answers

An abbreviated sidecar result can look like:

{
  "available_columns": ["Quantity", "Price", "Country"],
  "sample_data": [
    {"Quantity": 12, "Price": 6.95, "Country": "United Kingdom"}
  ],
  "column_semantics": {
    "Quantity": {
      "null_ratio": 0.0,
      "cardinality": 500,
      "sample_values": [12],
      "data_type": "int",
      "semantic_type": "numeric"
    }
  }
}

This output is illustrative and abbreviated; each listed column normally has a column_semantics entry.

docs.title: What the desktop sends
docs.text:
The current Ask Queries serializer requests the full sidecar summary, then sends these fields to conversation endpoints:

  • available_columns
  • column_semantics
  • total_rows
  • total_rows_read

It currently omits top-level sample_data. However, column_semantics can still contain sample_values. Direct API callers and benchmark clients pass their supplied metadata object through unchanged, so they may include sample_data as well.

This distinction matters for privacy statements: nolainquery does not send the full file or its local path to the Cloud API, but a sketch may contain actual values. Inspect the request you send if those values are sensitive.

docs.title: How cloud stages use it
docs.text:
The conversation classifier receives column names. Metadata-only answers use column names, row counts, and type information when present. Semantic analysis reads column_semantics: routing compares terms with column names, types, descriptions or meanings supplied by a caller, and up to three sample values. Specialist prompts receive a reduced form containing selected statistics and up to three sample_values.

Once generation is admitted, the worker receives the complete metadata object from the request. The Cloud API does not open or execute the local dataset; generated Pandas code and the optional dag artifact return to the local engine for execution.

For request fields and endpoints, continue to Calling the Cloud API. For the privacy boundary behind this contract, see The system philosophy.

docs.title: Query costs
docs.text:
Earlier chapters explained that you pay for reasoning work, not for running your file, and that a question is often several model calls. This chapter is the measurement: what 50 hard retail-invoice questions actually charged, on specific models, with and without a computation graph.

These are observed execution costs, not modeled case tables. Each run used the desktop conversation loop, a local Pandas engine, and the dataset recorded in that run’s parameters.txt. Credits are the product’s charged credits, not US dollars. The current default is 1,000 credits per dollar plus a 100% surplus; see Credits for the formula.

Worker token totals are included. Conversation-side calls (classification, semantic reading, optional narrative) are not. A live question can therefore cost a little more than the figures below.

When semantic analysis returned a clarification, the benchmark automatically selected the first offered interpretation for every ambiguous term and resent the question. That deterministic shortcut is useful for unattended runs, but it may not represent the interpretation a user would choose.

docs.title: GPT-5.6 Luna, Pandas only
docs.text:
Run configuration: Pandas-only run, GPT-5.6 Luna

  • 50 queries; 49 code executions succeeded (98%).
  • 204 credits were charged: 4.08 average, 4 median, and 8 maximum per query.
  • No Pandas, sandbox, runtime, or compiler retries occurred.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, Pandas only
docs.text:
Run configuration: Pandas-only run, DeepSeek V4 Flash

  • 50 queries; 35 code executions succeeded (70%).
  • 138 credits were charged: 2.76 average, 2 median, and 8 maximum per query.
  • 23 Pandas retries occurred: 21 sandbox retries and 2 runtime repairs.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: GPT-5.6 Luna, Pandas plus DAG
docs.text:
Run configuration: Pandas + DAG run, GPT-5.6 Luna

  • 50 queries; all 50 code executions succeeded (100%).
  • 45 DAG executions succeeded (90%).
  • 1,942 credits were charged: 38.84 average, 42 median, and 50 maximum per query.
  • 1 Pandas retry and 1 sandbox retry occurred; no runtime retries occurred.
  • Pandas and DAG outputs matched for 12 of 38 comparable queries (31.58%).
  • 87 compiler retries occurred, averaging 1.74 per query.
  • Ground-truth comparison was unavailable.

docs.title: What these runs show
docs.text:
• Adding DAG compilation greatly increased observed cost in this sample: 38.84 average credits versus 4.08 for GPT-5.6 Luna without a DAG.
  • The successful code rate was higher with the DAG run, but DAG execution was not perfect and its output matched Pandas in only 31.58% of comparable cases.
  • The DeepSeek run was cheaper, but its 70% code success rate and 23 retries show that cost alone does not describe the user experience.

These are measurements from one 50-query slice of the hard retail-invoice questions, on one dataset and the recorded configurations. They are not a price guarantee or a quality benchmark for other datasets, prompts, model versions, or deployments. None of the three runs had ground-truth answers, so accuracy against a known correct answer cannot be concluded. Pandas–DAG agreement measures two executors against each other, not correctness.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
The benchmark instructions and output-file definitions are in Custom benchmark README. The raw statistics are available in each linked run directory:

  • DAG run statistics
  • DeepSeek run statistics
  • GPT-5.6 Luna run statistics

Worker token totals and per-call billing fields are exposed in the benchmark JSON. Conversation classification, semantic reading, and optional answer framing are not included in these run totals.

These figures are a measurement, not a promise. For the formula behind the credits, return to Credits.
